title: "City-traffic-M: congestion and volume on 18 October 2024"
lang: en

    self_contained: true

params:
  dataset: "data/metropolis-real.json.gz"
  time_index: 55
---
City-traffic-M contains 720 roads on 18 October 2024. The day has 96
fifteen-minute intervals from 00:00 to 24:00, with the last interval starting
at 23:45. Each road has volume, speed and a descriptive congestion index.
The initial map interval starts at 13:30.

## Map and data

The map supports pan, zoom, playback and interval selection. Congestion and
volume have separate display modes. Road popups show the selected interval's
values alongside the road's reference speed and static attributes. A daily
trend accompanies the map, with a cursor at the selected interval.

The HTML embeds the traffic data, offline OSM geometry and Leaflet 1.9.4.
The documentation panel contains the preparation method, field definitions,
statistics and reference figures. The reference maps and summary below use
13:30; the map readouts follow the selected interval.

## Source and data preparation

The dataset metadata identifies `mightyneghbor/city-traffic-benchmarks`,
version 4. Its source files are `city-traffic-M-raw-static-features.parquet`,
`city-traffic-M-raw-volume.parquet` and `city-traffic-M-raw-speed.parquet`.
The snapshot provenance identifies the export
`city_traffic_M_osm_congestion_sample.html` and its companion JavaScript.

Snapshot preparation validates the JSON value assigned to
`window.CITY_TRAFFIC_OSM_SAMPLE` and places it in
`data/metropolis-real.json.gz`. The object contains road attributes, ordered
measurement arrays, frame summaries and metadata. The preparation code takes
the JavaScript export as input:

```{r preparation, eval=FALSE}
source_js <- 'city_traffic_M_osm_congestion_sample.js'
source_lines <- readLines(source_js, warn=FALSE, encoding='UTF-8')
pattern <- '^\\s*window\\.CITY_TRAFFIC_OSM_SAMPLE\\s*=\\s*'
payload <- sub(';\\s*$', '', sub(pattern, '',
               grep(pattern, source_lines, value=TRUE)))
stopifnot(length(payload)==1L, jsonlite::validate(payload))
provenance <- jsonlite::toJSON(list(
  source_html=sub('\\.js$','.html',basename(source_js)),
  source_js=basename(source_js), source_md5=unname(tools::md5sum(source_js))),
  auto_unbox=TRUE)
artifact <- paste0('{"schema_version":1,"source":"metropolis","provenance":',
                   provenance,',"payload":{"data":',payload,'}}')
output_file <- 'data/metropolis-real.json.gz'
stopifnot(!file.exists(output_file))
dir.create(dirname(output_file), recursive=TRUE, showWarnings=FALSE)
con <- gzfile(output_file, 'wt')
tryCatch(writeLines(artifact, con, useBytes=TRUE), finally=close(con))
```

The HTML build reads this packaged snapshot and `data/osm-basemap.json.gz`.
`map-template.html` defines the map interface and includes Leaflet's script,
styles and license. `run.R` renders this R Markdown document in a temporary
directory and embeds it with both datasets in `metropolis-traffic-maps.html`.

The source construction uses volume ranking and a 34 by 22 spatial grid for
road selection. Three five-minute observations form each fifteen-minute
average. Interpolation in both directions and zero filling occur before the
export. The per-road speed reference is the 90th percentile of nonzero speed
over the source observation period. These construction choices define the
snapshot's measurement and sampling conventions.

## Fields and coverage

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace('bdynets', quietly=TRUE)) {
  package_file <- 'bdynets_0.1.0.tar.gz'
  if (!file.exists(package_file)) stop('Bundled bdynets source package is absent')
  package_library <- tempfile('traffic-r-library-')
  dir.create(package_library)
  .libPaths(c(package_library, .libPaths()))
  install.packages(package_file, repos=NULL, type='source',
                   lib=package_library, quiet=TRUE)
  if (!requireNamespace('bdynets', quietly=TRUE))
    stop('Bundled bdynets package installation failed')
}
library(bdynets)
source('osm-figures.R')
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path=file.path(tempdir(),'metropolis-figure-'),message=FALSE)
```

```{r data}
x <- read_traffic_data(params$dataset)
meta <- x$data$metadata
stopifnot(x$source=='metropolis', !isTRUE(meta$synthetic),
          meta$sampleDay=='2024-10-18', length(x$data$frames)==96L,
          meta$frameIntervalMinutes==15L,
          x$data$frames[[1]]$time=='2024-10-18 00:00',
          x$data$frames[[96]]$time=='2024-10-18 23:45')
knitr::kable(data.frame(roads=length(x$data$segments), frames=length(x$data$frames),
                       minutes_per_frame=meta$frameIntervalMinutes))
```

| Field | Definition |
|---|---|
| `schema_version`, `source`, `provenance` | Wrapper format, dataset identifier and source filename/checksums. |
| `metadata` | Source, date, aggregation rule, road-selection method, speed reference and display scales. |
| `bounds` | Minimum and maximum latitude/longitude values. |
| `segments` | Road IDs, endpoint coordinates, length, region, category, edge type, speed-limit code/label, reference speed and selection volume statistic. |
| `frames[].i`, `time` | Zero-based interval number and source-clock start label. |
| `frames[].volume`, `speed`, `congestion` | Road arrays in `segments` order. Volume and speed have two decimal places; congestion has three. |
| `congestionMean`, `congestionP95` | Per-frame congestion summaries across the 720 roads. |
| `meanVolume` | Per-frame mean volume across the 720 roads. |
| `meanSpeed`, `active` | Mean speed over positive-volume roads, and the number of those roads. |

`freeFlowSpeed` is the per-road speed reference. `maxVolume` is a column
statistic from the volume file's first row group used during road selection;
it is not the maximum for the displayed day.

The metadata leaves the formal volume unit, timezone and CRS unspecified.
Speed labels use km/h. Interpreting the endpoint coordinates as longitude and
latitude places the roads near Yekaterinburg; the source metadata does not
provide a publisher-confirmed city name.

## Maps and daily trends

```{r figures, fig.width=9, fig.height=7, out.width='100%'}
figures <- traffic_osm_figures(params$dataset, 'metropolis',
                          time_index=params$time_index)
```

R index 55 corresponds to JavaScript index 54 and 13:30, the interval with the
highest total congestion in this day. Congestion uses the road-level index.
Volume color intensity is `volume / 69.33`, clipped to one, where 69.33 is the
whole-day volume p95. Both modes use green, amber and red, with line width
increasing with intensity.

The congestion definition is:

```text
congestion = clip(1 - speed / road_p90_speed, 0, 1)
             * clip(log1p(volume) / log1p(day_volume_p95), 0, 1)
```

The map reads `frames[].congestion`. Recalculation from rounded speed and
volume can give different values. Daily trends use `congestionMean` and
`meanVolume`. The congestion-p95 readout describes the selected interval;
the volume-p95 readout is the whole-day display reference.

Traffic uses Web Mercator for display. Road geometry consists of the endpoint
lines in `segments`. Dark casings distinguish the traffic lines from the
background. The two daily trends cover all 96 intervals.

## Selected-frame statistics

```{r summary}
selected_frame <- x$data$frames[[params$time_index]]
statistics <- unlist(selected_frame[c('congestionMean','congestionP95',
                                     'meanSpeed','meanVolume','active')])
knitr::kable(data.frame(statistic=names(statistics), value=unname(statistics)))
```

The reference interval starts at `r selected_frame$time`. Its mean congestion
is `r selected_frame$congestionMean`, mean volume is
`r selected_frame$meanVolume`, and mean speed is `r selected_frame$meanSpeed`,
with `r selected_frame$active` positive-volume roads. The table reads frame
summary fields; it does not recompute them from rounded road arrays.

## Offline basemap

`data/osm-basemap.json.gz` contains generalized roads, water polygons and place
labels from the Protomaps OSM archive dated 20 October 2026. The extract uses
zoom 11 and the traffic extent plus a 0.02-degree margin. `download_osm.py`
contains the extraction procedure. Cache provenance includes the archive URL,
retrieval time, tile hashes and a geometry checksum.

OSM supplies geographic context. The congestion calculation uses the traffic
attributes and reference speeds. Place labels are spaced to reduce overlap.
The basemap date and traffic date refer to separate data sources.

Map data: [OpenStreetMap contributors](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright),
via [Protomaps](https://docs.protomaps.com/basemaps/downloads), ODbL Produced Work.

## Build and figure export

`Rscript run.R` builds the HTML from this folder. R dependencies are `jsonlite`,
`rmarkdown`, `knitr`, `magrittr` and `bdynets`; HTML conversion uses Pandoc.
`bdynets_0.1.0.tar.gz` contains the version 0.1.0 source package and license.
The entrypoint uses that local archive in a temporary R library when the
package is absent. Viewing the HTML requires a current browser.

R indices run from 1 to 96. Index 55 starts at 13:30; index 33 starts at 08:00.
Figure-export functions have the following form:

```{r export-example, eval=FALSE}
plot_traffic_osm(traffic_frame(x, time_index=33L, metric='volume'),
                 read_osm_basemap())
plot(traffic_trend(x, metric='congestion', time_index=33L))
traffic_osm_figures(params$dataset, 'metropolis', time_index=33L,
                output_dir='output/metropolis-0800')
```

`osm-figures.R` provides PDF/PNG maps, trends and source records. Basemap
preparation uses Python packages `requests`, `pmtiles` and
`mapbox-vector-tile`. The HTML build and figure export use the packaged data
and cache.

## Interpretation

The maps and trends describe the selected 720 roads. Interpolation and zero
filling mean that displayed zeros do not identify raw missing observations.
The speed reference can include observations outside the displayed day, which
matters when interpreting a retrospective congestion index as a predictor.
This snapshot contains road-level measurements; individual vehicle paths and
validated directed adjacency are absent. It does not identify causal
congestion origins.
